core_obligations: Reformulate (proof lines 14207-14214): with K^vee the dual of K one has Hom_{D(O)}(K, M) = H^0(X, K^vee tensor^L M) functorially in M; since the tensor product with K^vee commutes with direct sums, it suffices to show that the derived global sections commute with the relevant direct sums.
Part (a) (proof lines 14216-14219): after the reformulation this is the lower-compactness lemma applied with U = X, using the bounded below setting.

Part (b) (proof lines 14221-14228): since R Gamma(X, K) = R Hom(O, K) and the cohomology functors commute with direct sums by the colimit lemma under the three hypotheses, this is the compactness criterion for j_!O_X.
proof_roadmap: Rewrite the Hom groups through the dual and reduce to commutation of derived global sections with direct sums.
Apply the bounded below compactness criterion with U = X for part (a).
Apply the bounded compactness criterion for part (b), using the commutation of cohomology with direct sums.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that a perfect object is compact in the bounded below derived category under three hypotheses on quasi-compactness of objects and coverings, and in the whole derived category when the site has finite cohomological dimension (statement lines 14180-14204). The proof (proof lines 14206-14228) rewrites the Hom groups via the dual of K, reducing to commutation of the derived global sections with direct sums, and then applies the two compactness criteria with U = X. H2: one reformulation plus two applications, written out.
